findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves, before any firstmate detail. Within a few lines they can say what this is and why it matters.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page explains why a newcomer to Athena lands on a study of a different project. That heads off the likely confusion, "why is the Athena page about firstmate?"
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit... This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: The next step is concrete: what you need first, the clone command, the install command, and a first command with what to expect. The header links straight to it, so a newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "./setup.sh" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link sits in the header next to the newcomer's next step but is meant for the project owner. A first-time visitor is told something is "waiting for your decision" that has nothing to do with them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page says Athena records cost and a reviewer verdict, but it never shows the cost, models or verdict behind this study. The one Athena output a newcomer can see here does not show the accountability it promises.
findings.source: Lede: "records what each step cost" and "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: The page defines "agent" as firstmate's deciding AI and never a worker. Yet in the relaunch text (and claim c18, "replaces the running agent"), "agent" means the worker being replaced, which breaks the page's own rule.
findings.source: "Firstmate's own deciding AI, called the agent on this page and never a worker" vs. "If a relaunch fails after the old agent was stopped, the prior durable record is restored and the report says no agent is running."

findings.text: t9 (ready → reopened) is listed as changing places-held, but the t9 card says nothing about places. A careful reader cannot tell what t9 does to the counter.
findings.source: Counters: "places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11"

findings.text: Captain, yolo, green, red, in scope and home are each defined twice, in nearly the same words. This adds length to a page that is already dense for someone who came mainly to learn about Athena.

The page is honest about gaps: what it could not find, and that nothing was run ("Limits of this study", f1 and f3). That makes the study more credible to a newcomer judging whether Athena's output can be trusted.
findings.source: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: This mentions a studies/ folder without saying which repository it is in or linking to it. A newcomer cannot follow it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
